items.title: server: wait for MCP handshake before platform storage (#1255, #1276)
items.basis: TECH-SPEC.md:270 already routes #1296 to GP1, and ADR-0007 states the v2 protocol is stateless (no initialize/initialized handshake; client info comes from each request's _meta), which removes the race this issue describes at the design level. round1 gave this verdict with no archaeology; archaeology below confirms it is a real, previously-patched race class, not a one-off.

archaeology.INTRODUCED_BY: fd4f89a5 / 9c28ff63 fix(pi): retry MCP bridge initialize on slow handshake (#647), Wed May 20 2026
archaeology.ORIGINAL_INTENT: commit message: 'When the spawned MCP child is slow to start (cold NFS home dir, first JIT compile of server.bundle.mjs, constrained CI), initialize can exceed the 60s ceiling... Before this fix, bootstrapMCPTools propagated the rejection up to extension.ts, which logged once and ran the rest of the session with no ctx_* tools registered.' Fix added bounded retry (MAX_INIT_RETRIES=2) with backoff before giving up.
archaeology.REGRESSION_RISK: v1 needed a retry/backoff layer because platform storage (ctx_stats/SessionDB) was reachable before the handshake settled, racing with a slow child process. ADR-0007's stateless design removes the handshake as a gate entirely, but if any v2 code path still reads 'platform storage' keyed off connection state rather than per-request _meta, the same slow-start race reappears without the v1 retry logic to mask it.
archaeology.SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: no fallback chain (owner decision); the GP1 contract test must assert platform/session identity is read per-request from _meta, never from a stored handshake flag, so a slow spawn cannot silently poison or delay storage.

items.fix: No doc change needed; add one line to GP1's test description (TECH-SPEC.md:270 area) that the contract test must include a slow-handshake / delayed-initialize fixture, given this is a recurring v1 bug class (#647, #1296).

items.title: hooks: route quoted curl/wget stdout destinations
items.basis: ADR-0008 replaces v1's regex-based curl/wget classifier with a real shell parser specifically to fix quoting bugs (#1221 cited directly: 'curl inside quotes'). DECISIONS-r3.md Q5 keeps the #166 silent/verbose curl checks but moves the implementation off regex. round1 gave this a verdict with no archaeology; archaeology below shows the exact v1 code and bug class being replaced.
items.evidence: docs/v2/adr/0008-enforcement-rewrite-and-cap.md:25 ('Regexes over a quote-stripped string' -> 'Own shell parser... no regex'); docs/v2/review/DECISIONS-r3.md:11

archaeology.INTRODUCED_BY: 2731ca25 feat: allow curl/wget with silent file-output, block stdout floods (#166), Sun Mar 22 2026
archaeology.ORIGINAL_INTENT: commit message: 'Allow when ALL conditions met: 1. Output to file (-o, --output, >, >>) 2. NOT stdout alias (-o -, /dev/stdout) 3. Silent flag present... 4. No verbose/trace flags.' Implemented as whitespace-anchored regex in hooks/core/routing.mjs:745-765, e.g. /\s(-o|--output)\s+(-|\/dev\/stdout)(\s|$)/.
archaeology.REGRESSION_RISK: the regex requires a literal space before the flag value and does not handle quoted arguments (e.g. curl -o "/dev/stdout") or --output=value form; a quoted or `=`-joined destination can slip past the stdout-alias check and be wrongly allowed, or a quoted safe file path can be wrongly flagged as dangerous. This is the same bug class #1221 names for other commands ('curl inside quotes, grep patterns, heredocs'). If v2 ships any regex fallback instead of the planned parser, #1299 reopens verbatim.
archaeology.SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: no regex as the decision mechanism (owner decision, ADR-0008); the lexer/parser must evaluate the actual parsed argv tokens for -o/--output/--output-document/-O regardless of quoting, matching the #166 intent (file output + silent + no verbose + not a stdout alias).

items.fix: None needed on current text; ADR-0008 already encodes the fix. Recommend adding '#1299' next to the existing #1221/#166/#817 citations in ADR-0008 row 'Regexes over a quote-stripped string' so the doc's own issue trail is complete.

items.title: fix(codex): isolate project context for concurrent chats
items.basis: TECH-SPEC.md:271 maps #1302 to GP7 and GP7's row already lists #1302 among the issues its test must cover ('2 worktrees x 2 sessions x 2 agents; identity shared per repo'). round1 gave this a verdict with no archaeology; archaeology below shows two separate, already-patched v1 bugs in the same project-identity area, both relevant to what GP7 must not regress.

archaeology.INTRODUCED_BY: ab73792c fix(env-leak): resolvePiWorkspaceDir() rejects ~/.pi/ as project root (closes #545 partial), Tue May 12 2026; ddd3b5bb fix(stats): plugin-install-path projectDir poisoning after /ctx-upgrade, Sun May 10 2026
archaeology.ORIGINAL_INTENT: ab73792c: 'Pi's extension previously used PI_CONFIG_DIR (=~/.pi) as the project anchor, collapsing every Pi session into a single phantom workspace.' ddd3b5bb: 'After Claude Code runs /ctx-upgrade, it kills + respawns the MCP server with cwd set to the plugin install dir. The legacy start.mjs then set CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR = originalCwd, poisoning every downstream ctx_stats / SessionDB / hash computation.'
archaeology.REGRESSION_RISK: both are the same failure family as #1302: one host-specific env var or cwd value gets used as the project anchor without validating it against known-bad paths (home dir, plugin cache dir), and two live sessions/chats collapse onto one identity. For Codex specifically, concurrent chats sharing one process could repeat this if v2 derives project identity from a single global env var instead of per-connection/per-request state.
archaeology.SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: no fallback chain (owner decision, same as Q11/ADR-0007); GP7's 2x2x2 test matrix must include a same-process concurrent-chat case for Codex specifically (not just separate worktrees/sessions), since that is the literal #1302 title and is not obviously the same shape as the worktree/session cases already named.

items.fix: GP7's test description (TECH-SPEC.md:295) lists worktrees/sessions/agents as the 3 axes; add 'concurrent chats within one Codex process' as an explicit 4th case so #1302 is not assumed covered by the other three.
